page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.8xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance built on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, the instance delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration features 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. It supports AVX and AVX-512 extensions alongside hardware AES encryption and bit-manipulation instruction sets.

The instance is provisioned with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs included. Local disk storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached cloud disks for all persistent storage operations. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps, providing sufficient network throughput for inter-service communication and remote storage access.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent middle-tier throughput for parallel workloads alongside modest single-thread execution rates. Synthetic CPU tests show average multi-core capability, recording 28,022.52 in stress-ng multi-core and 9,949.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Single-core results place in the lower quartile, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1,085.0 and 1,313.98 in stress-ng single-core. Memory bandwidth aligns with platform averages, reaching 109.41 GB/s on large-block reads and 48.07 GB/s on writes.

Given its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation, the instance favors high-concurrency tasks where aggregate core count takes priority over per-thread latency or heavy per-thread RAM utilization. The hardware profile is appropriate for multi-threaded build environments, static web serving clusters, batch processing, and horizontally scaled container workloads.

It includes 64.0 GB of RAM, representing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server has no bundled local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and standard network infrastructure with a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark performance reflects lower-tier single-core speeds offset by average multi-core and memory throughput across Geekbench, stress-ng, and PassMark tests. With 32 execution threads and modest per-core RAM, this instance functions well for multi-threaded batch operations, code compilation, microservices, and static web serving.
